ACME Corporation — Data Classification Standard

The company operates four data classification tiers: Public, Internal, Confidential and Restricted. Every data asset must carry exactly one classification at any given time.
Data classified as Restricted must be encrypted both at rest and in transit, and may only be processed on managed company devices. Transfer to removable media is blocked by policy.
Confidential data may not be shared outside the company without a signed non-disclosure agreement in place. The legal team maintains the register of executed agreements.
Classification labelling is mandatory on all documents, datasets and system records. Unlabelled assets discovered during audit are escalated to the asset owner for immediate remediation.
Where no classification has been assigned, data defaults to Internal and must be handled accordingly. The default does not relieve the asset owner of the obligation to classify explicitly.
Classifications are reviewed annually by the asset owner, or sooner where the sensitivity of the data changes. The review date is recorded against the asset in the data catalogue.

ACME Corporation — Data Retention Schedule

Payroll records are retained for 7 years from the end of the tax year to which they relate. Retention is required for statutory audit and is not subject to early deletion requests.
Customer records are retained for 6 years after the end of the customer relationship. At the end of this period records are deleted automatically unless subject to a live legal hold.
CCTV footage is retained for 30 days and then overwritten automatically. Footage required for an investigation must be extracted and preserved within the retention window.
Corporate email is retained for 3 years from the date of sending or receipt. Mailboxes of departed employees are preserved for the remainder of the retention period and then deleted.
Recruitment records for unsuccessful candidates are retained for 12 months from the date of the hiring decision. Candidates may request earlier deletion at any point during this period.
System and application logs are retained for 13 months to support security investigation and trend analysis. Logs are stored in an append-only store and cannot be edited after write.

ACME Corporation — Data Subject Requests and Deletion

A data subject access request must receive a substantive response within 30 calendar days of receipt. The clock starts on the date the request is received, not the date it is assigned.

Where a request is complex or involves multiple systems, the response period may be extended by a further 60 days. The data subject must be informed of the extension and its reason within the original 30-day window.
The identity of the requester must be verified before any personal data is disclosed. Verification uses two independent identifiers and is recorded against the request file.
No fee is charged for a first data subject access request. A reasonable administrative fee may be applied to repeat requests from the same individual within a 6-month period.
Approved deletion requests are executed within 30 days of approval across all production systems and backups scheduled for the next rotation. A deletion certificate is issued to the requester.
Any request that cannot be fulfilled within the standard process is escalated to the Data Protection Officer for decision. The Officer's determination is recorded with reasons in the request file.

ACME Corporation — Travel Booking and Class of Travel

Business travel must be booked at least 14 days before departure. Bookings made inside this window require written justification from the traveller's department head and are reported in the monthly travel summary.
Flights with a scheduled duration under 6 hours are booked in economy class. This applies regardless of grade, destination or time of departure.
Flights with a scheduled duration above 6 hours may be booked in business class for employees at manager grade and above. All other employees travel premium economy on long-haul routes.

All travel must be booked through the approved corporate booking platform. Travel booked directly with airlines, hotels or third-party sites is not reimbursed except where the platform is demonstrably unavailable.
Where a rail journey of under 4 hours is available between origin and destination, rail is the required mode of travel in preference to air. Exceptions require department head approval.
Travel cancellations must be notified to the booking platform at least 48 hours before departure to avoid charges. Unnotified cancellations are recharged to the originating department's budget.

ACME Corporation — Per Diem and Subsistence

The domestic per diem allowance is $60 per full day of travel, covering meals and incidental costs. A full day is any period of travel exceeding ten hours away from the normal place of work.
The international per diem allowance is $95 per full day. Where the destination appears on the high-cost cities schedule, a supplement of $30 per day is applied automatically.
Receipts are not required for expenditure covered by the per diem allowance. Per diem is claimed by recording travel dates and destination in the expense system without itemisation.
Hotel accommodation is capped at $180 per night for domestic travel. Bookings above the cap require advance approval and must be justified by the absence of compliant alternatives.
An incidentals allowance of $15 per night is payable in addition to per diem where the trip involves an overnight stay. This covers laundry, connectivity and personal calls.
Client entertainment during business travel requires pre-approval from a department head irrespective of value. Post-hoc approval is not granted and unapproved entertainment spend is not reimbursed.

ACME Corporation — Visa, Insurance and Traveller Safety

Corporate travel insurance covers every employee automatically on business travel, with no individual registration required. Cover includes medical treatment, repatriation and trip disruption.
Visa application fees, associated appointment costs and expedited processing charges are reimbursed in full where the visa is required for business travel. Receipts must be submitted with the claim.

Travel to destinations on the high-risk schedule requires written clearance from the corporate security team before booking. Clearance considers current advisories and the business necessity of the trip.

Travellers must register an emergency contact and their itinerary in the traveller tracking system before departure. The record enables location-based notification during a disruption or security event.

Vaccinations and antimalarial medication required for a business destination are paid for by the company. Employees arrange appointments through the occupational health provider and claim the cost as an expense.

A 24-hour travel assistance line is available to all travellers for medical, security and logistical emergencies while abroad. The number is printed on the corporate travel card issued to every traveller.
